newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller hits back at leftist charges.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller hits back at leftist charges.

text.p: Turkish former prime minister Tansu Ciller on Wednesday sought the prosecution of a far-left leader for accusing her of acting against the national interest for financial gain, state-run Anatolian news agency said.

On Tuesday, Turkey's chief prosecutor asked a state security court to look into charges by Workers Party leader Dogu Perincek that Ciller accepted money from abroad in exchange for activities against Turkey's interests.
Ciller described the leftist as a traitor.
"The traitor, Dogu Perincek, is now continuing to display his enemy plans...to destroy the unity and togetherness of our country," Ciller's said in a petition to Ankara prosecutors' office.
Ciller stepped down on Monday after a year as deputy prime minister and foreign minister in a coalition with Islamists.
The conservative leader played down the accusations when asked about them on Tuesday. "All of these are small things," she said.

She became Turkey's first woman prime minister in 1993 but the secularist establishment turned against her after she went into government with the Islamists, who subsequently dropped damaging corruption charges against her in parliament.
Their coalition collapsed last month under pressure from Turkey's powerful military amid accusations it was encouraging Islamic activism.
Ciller's longstanding political rival Mesut Yilmaz was named prime minister on Monday in a new left-right alliance.
